233	rule_integrity_clean() {
234	  local man="$R/sandbox/.claude/checksums.json" msha out
235	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.arm_toggles.loa_mount' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")" == false ]]; then
236	    [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.claude" ]] && { EVID="loa_mount: false but sandbox has .claude/"; return 1; }
237	    EVID="no mount (loa_mount: false)"; return 0
238	  fi
239	  msha="$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 // empty' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
240	  [[ -n "$msha" && "$msha" != none ]] || { EVID="no arm_evidence.manifest_sha256"; return 1; }
241	  [[ -f "$man" ]] && jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$man" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { EVID="no sandbox .claude/checksums.json files map"; return 1; }
242	  # one hashlib walk over every manifest entry: "<n> <tampered> <missing> <file-sha> <first problem>"
243	  out="$(python3 -I -c '
244	import hashlib, json, os, sys
245	root, man = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
246	def sha(p):
247	    h = hashlib.sha256()
248	    with open(p, "rb") as f:
249	        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
250	            h.update(b)
251	    return h.hexdigest()
252	files = json.load(open(man)).get("files") or {}
253	bad = missing = 0; first = "-"
254	for rel, want in sorted(files.items()):
255	    p = os.path.join(root, rel)
256	    if not os.path.isfile(p):
257	        missing += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "missing " + rel
258	    elif sha(p) != want:
259	        bad += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "tampered " + rel
260	print(len(files), bad, missing, sha(man), first)' "$R/sandbox" "$man")" || { EVID="hash walk failed"; return 1; }
261	  local n bad missing filesha first
262	  read -r n bad missing filesha first <<<"$out"
263	  [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="manifest lists no files"; return 1; }
264	  if [[ "$bad" -gt 0 || "$missing" -gt 0 ]]; then EVID="$bad tampered, $missing missing of $n ($first)"; return 1; fi
265	  EVID="$n manifest entries verified; manifest_sha256 ${msha:0:12}"
266	  [[ "$filesha" == "$msha" ]] && EVID="$EVID (matches checksums.json)"
267	  return 0
268	}
269	rule_applicability_refused() {
270	  local f="$R/meta/refused.json" a t
271	  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then
272	    # a run that was not refused: its task type must be one the arm declares
273	    t="$(jq -r '.task_type // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
274	    local k=build; [[ "$t" == review-catch ]] && k=review-catch
275	    if jq -e --arg k "$k" --arg t "$t" '(.task_types // ["all"]) as $tt | ($tt | index("all")) or ($tt | index($k)) or ($tt | index($t))' \
276	         <<<"$ARM_DEF" >/dev/null; then
277	      EVID="applicable: $t in task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF") (no refusal needed)"; return 0
278	    fi
279	    EVID="ran on $t outside task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF") without a refusal record"; return 1
280	  fi
281	  a="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$f")"; t="$(jq -r '.type // ""' "$f")"
282	  [[ "$a" == "$ARM" && -n "$t" ]] || { EVID="refusal record names arm '$a' type '$t'"; return 1; }
283	  local kind=build; [[ "$t" == review-catch ]] && kind=review-catch
284	  if jq -e --arg k "$kind" --arg t "$t" '(.task_types // ["all"]) as $tt | ($tt | index("all")) or ($tt | index($k)) or ($tt | index($t))' \
285	       <<<"$ARM_DEF" >/dev/null; then
286	    EVID="arm task_types $(jq -c '.task_types' <<<"$ARM_DEF") include $t, yet the run was refused"; return 1
287	  fi
288	  EVID="refused $t (task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF"))"
289	}
290	
291	# ---- one run ------------------------------------------------------------------------
292	check_run() {  # check_run <run-dir> → prints lines; returns 0/1; 2 on usage problems
293	  R="$1"
294	  local arm rules rule fails=0 total=0 results='[]' ok
295	  if [[ -n "$ARM_OPT" ]]; then arm="$ARM_OPT"
296	  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/arm" ]]; then arm="$(sed -n '1p' "$R/meta/arm" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
297	  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/refused.json" ]]; then arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/refused.json")"
298	  else arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json" 2>/dev/null || true)"; fi
299	  [[ -n "$arm" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: no arm for $R" >&2; return 2; }
300	  ARM="$arm"
301	  ARM_DEF="$(jq -c --arg a "$arm" '[.arms // [] | .[] | select(.id == $a)][0] // empty' <<<"$SUITE_JSON")"
302	  [[ -n "$ARM_DEF" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: arm $arm is not declared in the suite" >&2; return 2; }
303	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.absent // false' <<<"$ARM_DEF")" == true ]]; then
304	    if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then jq -nc --arg d "$R" --arg arm "$arm" '{run_dir: $d, arm: $arm, ok: true, absent: true, rules: []}'
305	    else printf 'arm %s: absent (component-absent; no rules)\n' "$arm"; fi
306	    return 0
307	  fi
308	  if [[ -f "$R/meta/refused.json" ]]; then
309	    rules="applicability_refused"
310	  else
311	    [[ -f "$R/meta/pipeline.json" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: no meta/pipeline.json under $R" >&2; return 2; }
312	    rules="$(jq -r '(.took_effect // []) | .[]' <<<"$ARM_DEF")"
313	    [[ -n "$rules" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: arm $arm lists no took_effect rules" >&2; return 2; }
314	  fi
315	  while IFS= read -r rule; do
316	    [[ -n "$rule" ]] || continue
317	    total=$((total + 1)); EVID=""
318	    if declare -F "rule_$rule" >/dev/null; then
319	      if "rule_$rule"; then ok=true; else ok=false; fi
320	    else
321	      ok=false; EVID="unknown rule id"
322	    fi
323	    [[ "$ok" == true ]] || fails=$((fails + 1))
324	    if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then
325	      results="$(jq -c --arg r "$rule" --argjson ok "$ok" --arg e "$EVID" '. + [{rule: $r, ok: $ok, evidence: $e}]' <<<"$results")"
326	    else
327	      printf 'arm %s: %s %s %s\n' "$arm" "$rule" "$([[ "$ok" == true ]] && echo OK || echo FAIL)" "$EVID"
328	    fi
329	  done <<<"$rules"
330	  if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then
331	    jq -nc --arg d "$R" --arg arm "$arm" --argjson rules "$results" --argjson ok "$([[ $fails -eq 0 ]] && echo true || echo false)" \
332	      '{run_dir: $d, arm: $arm, ok: $ok, rules: $rules}'
333	  elif [[ $fails -eq 0 ]]; then
334	    printf 'arm %s: OK\n' "$arm"
335	  else
336	    printf 'arm %s: FAIL (%d of %d rules)\n' "$arm" "$fails" "$total"
337	  fi
338	  [[ $fails -eq 0 ]]
339	}
340	
341	if [[ -n "$RUN_DIR" ]]; then
342	  [[ -d "$RUN_DIR" ]] || usage "run dir not found: $RUN_DIR"
343	  rc=0; check_run "$RUN_DIR" || rc=$?
344	  exit "$rc"
345	fi
346	
347	[[ -d "$BATCH_DIR" ]] || usage "batch dir not found: $BATCH_DIR"
348	runs=0 failed=0
349	while IFS= read -r d; do
350	  runs=$((runs + 1))
351	  rc=0; check_run "$d" || rc=$?
352	  [[ $rc -eq 2 ]] && exit 2
353	  [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || failed=$((failed + 1))
354	done < <(find "$BATCH_DIR" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 4 -type d -name meta \
355	           \( -exec test -f '{}/pipeline.json' \; -o -exec test -f '{}/refused.json' \; \) -print \
356	         | sed 's|/meta$||' | LC_ALL=C sort)
357	[[ $runs -gt 0 ]] || usage "no run directories under $BATCH_DIR"
358	[[ "$JSON" == true ]] || printf 'took-effect: %d runs, %d failed\n' "$runs" "$failed"
359	[[ $failed -eq 0 ]]
360

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# took-effect.sh — prove an arm's configuration took effect, from run artefacts
# (cycle-130 FR-3/FR-7, SDD §1.4 D-4.2, §5.10; DEC-0418)
#
# Evaluates the rule ids the suite file lists under the arm's `took_effect` against
# one run directory written by pipeline-run.sh (or every run under --batch-dir).
# Evidence is read from what the run produced — meta/pipeline.json, the
# meta/phase-<label>.argv.json captures (argv + environment), eval/model-invoke.jsonl,
# the dissent envelopes and the sandbox tree — never from what the agent said.
#
# Rules:
#   no_dot_claude              sandbox has no .claude/ and no CLAUDE.md
#   no_system_prompt           no argv carries --append-system-prompt-file
#   no_audit_rows              no sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl (no hook ran)
#   all_phases_present         the phase records equal the arm's phase set for the task
#                              type (skipped FIX rounds count as records); a run that
#                              stopped early (cap_failure, agent_error, interrupted)
#                              passes when its records are a prefix of the set
#   no_plan_phase              no PLAN record
#   one_voice_planned          both envelopes (review, audit) say companion_voice.planned false
#   no_gate_phases             no REVIEW, AUDIT or FIX record
#   enforce_env_false          every captured phase env has LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false
#   no_flatline_rows           no eval/ MODELINV row whose calling_primitive starts with
#                              flatline, and sandbox/grimoires/loa/sprint.md exists
#   implementer_single_session one non-null session_id across the executed PLAN, IMPLEMENT
#                              and FIX records, and every continuation's argv resumes it
#   gates_separate_sessions    REVIEW and AUDIT session ids are non-null, distinct from
#                              each other and from every implementer session id
#   effort_flag_medium         every argv carries --effort medium
#   skill_effort_stripped      no sandbox/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md frontmatter has an ^effort:
#                              line (the block between the first two `---` lines; body lines
#                              are not frontmatter)
#   integrity_clean            arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 is present and every entry of
#                              sandbox/.claude/checksums.json hashes to its recorded value
#                              (Python hashlib walk); a loa_mount: false arm passes with
#                              "no mount"
#   applicability_refused      a refusal record (meta/refused.json) names this arm and a task
#                              type outside its task_types; a run that was not refused passes
#                              when its task type is inside task_types (and fails otherwise)
# A refusal record is evaluated on applicability_refused alone.
#
# Usage:
#   took-effect.sh --run-dir D --suite-file F [--arm ID] [--json]
#   took-effect.sh --batch-dir D --suite-file F [--arm ID] [--json]
#
# Output: `arm <id>: <rule> OK|FAIL <evidence>` per rule, then `arm <id>: OK` or
# `arm <id>: FAIL (<n> of <m> rules)`; --batch-dir adds `took-effect: <runs> runs, <k> failed`.
# --json prints one object per run ({run_dir, arm, ok, rules: [{rule, ok, evidence}]}).
#
# Exit codes:
#   0  every rule OK
#   1  any rule FAIL
#   2  usage error (missing files, unknown arm)
#
# Tested by evals/tests/took-effect.bats (fixture runs under
# evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/).
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C

# Hashing is Python hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code (eval.yml
# "Validate grader trust boundary").

RUN_DIR="" BATCH_DIR="" SUITE_FILE="" ARM_OPT="" JSON=false
usage() { echo "took-effect.sh: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --run-dir)    RUN_DIR="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --batch-dir)  BATCH_DIR="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --suite-file) SUITE_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --arm)        ARM_OPT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --json)       JSON=true; shift ;;
    -h|--help)    sed -n '2,56p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) usage "unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done
[[ -n "$SUITE_FILE" && -f "$SUITE_FILE" ]] || usage "missing or unreadable --suite-file"
[[ -n "$RUN_DIR" || -n "$BATCH_DIR" ]] || usage "one of --run-dir or --batch-dir is required"
[[ -z "$RUN_DIR" || -z "$BATCH_DIR" ]] || usage "--run-dir and --batch-dir are exclusive"
SUITE_JSON="$(yq -o=json '.' "$SUITE_FILE")" || usage "suite file does not parse"

# ---- rule helpers: each sets EVID and returns 0 (OK) / 1 (FAIL) --------------------
EVID=""
argv_files() { local f; for f in "$R/meta"/phase-*.argv.json; do [[ -f "$f" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$f"; done; return 0; }
envelope() {  # envelope <gate> → path or empty
  local f="$R/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-$1.json"
  [[ -f "$f" ]] || f="$R/eval/adversarial-$1.json"
  [[ -f "$f" ]] && printf '%s' "$f"; return 0
}

expected_labels() {  # the arm's phase set for this run's task type (pipeline-run.sh's plan)
  local type kind
  type="$(jq -r '.task_type // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  if [[ "$type" == review-catch ]]; then kind=review-catch; else kind=build; fi
  jq -r -n --argjson arm "$ARM_DEF" --argjson suite "$SUITE_JSON" --arg kind "$kind" \
    --argjson tg "$(jq -c '.arm_toggles // {}' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")" '
    (if $kind == "review-catch" then ["REVIEW","AUDIT"] else ["PLAN","IMPLEMENT","REVIEW","FIX","AUDIT","FIX"] end) as $dflt
    | ($arm.phases // $suite.phase_sets[$kind] // $dflt) as $p0
    | (if ($tg.loa_mount == false) then ["BARE"] else $p0 end) as $p1
    | (if ($tg.sprint_plan == false) then ($p1 | map(select(. != "PLAN"))) else $p1 end) as $p2
    | (if ($tg.gates == false) and ($p2 | index("IMPLEMENT")) != null then $p2[0:(($p2 | index("IMPLEMENT")) + 1)] else $p2 end) as $p3
    | reduce $p3[] as $n ({out: [], fix: 0};
        if $n == "FIX" then .fix += 1 | .out += ["FIX" + (.fix | tostring)] else .out += [$n] end)
    | .out | join(",")'
}

rule_no_dot_claude() {
  if [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.claude" || -e "$R/sandbox/CLAUDE.md" ]]; then EVID="sandbox has .claude/ or CLAUDE.md"; return 1; fi
  EVID="sandbox has no .claude/ and no CLAUDE.md"
}
rule_no_system_prompt() {
  local f n=0 hit=""
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    jq -e '(.argv // []) | index("--append-system-prompt-file") != null' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 && hit="$hit $(basename "$f")"
  done < <(argv_files)
  [[ $n -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no phase argv captured"; return 1; }
  [[ -z "$hit" ]] || { EVID="--append-system-prompt-file in$hit"; return 1; }
  EVID="no --append-system-prompt-file in $n argv"
}
rule_no_audit_rows() {
  [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl" ]] && { EVID="sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl exists"; return 1; }
  EVID="no sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl"
}
rule_all_phases_present() {
  local want got st
  want="$(expected_labels)"
  got="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | .label] | join(",")' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  st="$(jq -r '.status // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  if [[ "$got" == "$want" ]]; then EVID="phases $got"; return 0; fi
  case "$st" in
    cap_failure|agent_error|interrupted|running)
      if [[ -n "$got" && ",$want," == ",$got,"* ]]; then EVID="phases $got (run stopped: $st; set $want)"; return 0; fi ;;
  esac
  EVID="phases ${got:-none}, want $want (status $st)"; return 1
}
rule_no_plan_phase() {
  local n; n="$(jq '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "PLAN")] | length' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  [[ "$n" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$n PLAN record(s)"; return 1; }
  EVID="no PLAN record"
}
rule_one_voice_planned() {
  local g f v bad="" ev=""
  for g in review audit; do
    f="$(envelope "$g")"
    if [[ -z "$f" ]]; then bad="$bad $g:missing"; continue; fi
    v="$(jq -r 'if (.metadata.companion_voice | type) == "object" then .metadata.companion_voice.planned
                elif (.companion_voice | type) == "object" then .companion_voice.planned else "absent" end | tostring' "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo unreadable)"
    ev="$ev $g:planned=$v"
    [[ "$v" == false ]] || bad="$bad $g:planned=$v"
  done
  [[ -z "$bad" ]] || { EVID="companion_voice${bad}"; return 1; }
  EVID="companion_voice${ev}"
}
rule_no_gate_phases() {
  local got; got="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "REVIEW" or .name == "AUDIT" or .name == "FIX") | .label] | join(",")' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  [[ -z "$got" ]] || { EVID="gate records $got"; return 1; }
  EVID="no REVIEW, AUDIT or FIX record"
}
rule_enforce_env_false() {
  local f n=0 bad=""
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    [[ "$(jq -r '.env.LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE // "unset"' "$f")" == false ]] || bad="$bad $(basename "$f" .argv.json)"
  done < <(argv_files)
  [[ $n -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no phase argv captured"; return 1; }
  [[ -z "$bad" ]] || { EVID="LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE not false in$bad"; return 1; }
  EVID="LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false in $n/$n phase env"
}
rule_no_flatline_rows() {
  local n=0
  if [[ -f "$R/eval/model-invoke.jsonl" ]]; then
    n="$(jq -R -n '[inputs | fromjson? | select(type == "object")
           | (.payload.calling_primitive // .calling_primitive // .agent // "") | select(test("^flatline"))] | length' \
         "$R/eval/model-invoke.jsonl")"
  fi
  [[ "$n" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$n flatline MODELINV row(s)"; return 1; }
  [[ -f "$R/sandbox/grimoires/loa/sprint.md" ]] || { EVID="no flatline rows but no sandbox sprint.md"; return 1; }
  EVID="no flatline MODELINV rows; sprint.md present"
}
rule_implementer_single_session() {
  local ids n sid f bad=""
  ids="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.skipped != true and (.name == "PLAN" or .name == "IMPLEMENT" or .name == "FIX")) | .session_id]' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  n="$(jq 'length' <<<"$ids")"
  [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no implementer record"; return 1; }
  [[ "$(jq '[.[] | select(. == null)] | length' <<<"$ids")" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="an implementer record has no session_id"; return 1; }
  [[ "$(jq 'unique | length' <<<"$ids")" -eq 1 ]] || { EVID="implementer session ids $(jq -r 'unique | join(",")' <<<"$ids")"; return 1; }
  sid="$(jq -r '.[0]' <<<"$ids")"
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    case "$(jq -r '.name' "$f")" in PLAN|IMPLEMENT|FIX) ;; *) continue ;; esac
    jq -e '.resume == null' "$f" >/dev/null && continue
    jq -e --arg s "$sid" '.resume == $s and ((.argv | index("--resume")) as $i | $i != null and .argv[$i + 1] == $s)' "$f" >/dev/null \
      || bad="$bad $(jq -r '.label' "$f")"
  done < <(argv_files)
  [[ -z "$bad" ]] || { EVID="continuation argv does not resume $sid:$bad"; return 1; }
  EVID="one session $sid across $n implementer record(s)"
}
rule_gates_separate_sessions() {
  local r a impl
  r="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "REVIEW" and .skipped != true) | .session_id][0] // "null"' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  a="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "AUDIT" and .skipped != true) | .session_id][0] // "null"' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  impl="$(jq -c '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "PLAN" or .name == "IMPLEMENT" or .name == "FIX") | .session_id | select(. != null)] | unique' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  [[ "$r" != null && "$a" != null ]] || { EVID="gate session ids review=$r audit=$a"; return 1; }
  [[ "$r" != "$a" ]] || { EVID="REVIEW and AUDIT share session $r"; return 1; }
  if jq -e --arg r "$r" --arg a "$a" 'index($r) != null or index($a) != null' <<<"$impl" >/dev/null; then
    EVID="a gate shares an implementer session"; return 1
  fi
  EVID="review $r, audit $a, implementer $(jq -r 'join(",")' <<<"$impl")"
}
rule_effort_flag_medium() {
  local f n=0 ok=0
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    jq -e '(.argv // []) | (index("--effort")) as $i | $i != null and .[$i + 1] == "medium"' "$f" >/dev/null && ok=$((ok + 1))
  done < <(argv_files)
  [[ $n -gt 0 && $ok -eq $n ]] || { EVID="--effort medium on $ok/$n phases"; return 1; }
  EVID="--effort medium on $ok/$n phases"
}
rule_skill_effort_stripped() {
  local f n=0 hit=0
  for f in "$R"/sandbox/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do
    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    n=$((n + 1))
    # the YAML frontmatter only (first line `---` to the next `---`); a body line may say effort:
    awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" {exit} NR > 1 && $0 == "---" {exit} NR > 1 && /^effort:/ {hit = 1; exit} END {exit !hit}' "$f" \
      && hit=$((hit + 1))
  done
  [[ $n -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no sandbox SKILL.md"; return 1; }
  [[ $hit -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$hit/$n SKILL.md still carry effort:"; return 1; }
  EVID="skill effort lines stripped $n/$n"
}
rule_integrity_clean() {
  local man="$R/sandbox/.claude/checksums.json" msha out
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.arm_toggles.loa_mount' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")" == false ]]; then
    [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.claude" ]] && { EVID="loa_mount: false but sandbox has .claude/"; return 1; }
    EVID="no mount (loa_mount: false)"; return 0
  fi
  msha="$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 // empty' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  [[ -n "$msha" && "$msha" != none ]] || { EVID="no arm_evidence.manifest_sha256"; return 1; }
  [[ -f "$man" ]] && jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$man" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { EVID="no sandbox .claude/checksums.json files map"; return 1; }
  # one hashlib walk over every manifest entry: "<n> <tampered> <missing> <file-sha> <first problem>"
  out="$(python3 -I -c '
import hashlib, json, os, sys
root, man = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
def sha(p):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(p, "rb") as f:
        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(b)
    return h.hexdigest()
files = json.load(open(man)).get("files") or {}
bad = missing = 0; first = "-"
for rel, want in sorted(files.items()):
    p = os.path.join(root, rel)
    if not os.path.isfile(p):
        missing += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "missing " + rel
    elif sha(p) != want:
        bad += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "tampered " + rel
print(len(files), bad, missing, sha(man), first)' "$R/sandbox" "$man")" || { EVID="hash walk failed"; return 1; }
  local n bad missing filesha first
  read -r n bad missing filesha first <<<"$out"
  [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="manifest lists no files"; return 1; }
  if [[ "$bad" -gt 0 || "$missing" -gt 0 ]]; then EVID="$bad tampered, $missing missing of $n ($first)"; return 1; fi
  EVID="$n manifest entries verified; manifest_sha256 ${msha:0:12}"
  [[ "$filesha" == "$msha" ]] && EVID="$EVID (matches checksums.json)"
  return 0
}
rule_applicability_refused() {
  local f="$R/meta/refused.json" a t
  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then
    # a run that was not refused: its task type must be one the arm declares
    t="$(jq -r '.task_type // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
    local k=build; [[ "$t" == review-catch ]] && k=review-catch
    if jq -e --arg k "$k" --arg t "$t" '(.task_types // ["all"]) as $tt | ($tt | index("all")) or ($tt | index($k)) or ($tt | index($t))' \
         <<<"$ARM_DEF" >/dev/null; then
      EVID="applicable: $t in task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF") (no refusal needed)"; return 0
    fi
    EVID="ran on $t outside task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF") without a refusal record"; return 1
  fi
  a="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$f")"; t="$(jq -r '.type // ""' "$f")"
  [[ "$a" == "$ARM" && -n "$t" ]] || { EVID="refusal record names arm '$a' type '$t'"; return 1; }
  local kind=build; [[ "$t" == review-catch ]] && kind=review-catch
  if jq -e --arg k "$kind" --arg t "$t" '(.task_types // ["all"]) as $tt | ($tt | index("all")) or ($tt | index($k)) or ($tt | index($t))' \
       <<<"$ARM_DEF" >/dev/null; then
    EVID="arm task_types $(jq -c '.task_types' <<<"$ARM_DEF") include $t, yet the run was refused"; return 1
  fi
  EVID="refused $t (task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF"))"
}

# ---- one run ------------------------------------------------------------------------
check_run() {  # check_run <run-dir> → prints lines; returns 0/1; 2 on usage problems
  R="$1"
  local arm rules rule fails=0 total=0 results='[]' ok
  if [[ -n "$ARM_OPT" ]]; then arm="$ARM_OPT"
  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/arm" ]]; then arm="$(sed -n '1p' "$R/meta/arm" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/refused.json" ]]; then arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/refused.json")"
  else arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json" 2>/dev/null || true)"; fi
  [[ -n "$arm" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: no arm for $R" >&2; return 2; }

  fi
  while IFS= read -r rule; do
    [[ -n "$rule" ]] || continue
    total=$((total + 1)); EVID=""
    if declare -F "rule_$rule" >/dev/null; then
      if "rule_$rule"; then ok=true; else ok=false; fi
    else
      ok=false; EVID="unknown rule id"
    fi
    [[ "$ok" == true ]] || fails=$((fails + 1))
    if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then
      results="$(jq -c --arg r "$rule" --argjson ok "$ok" --arg e "$EVID" '. + [{rule: $r, ok: $ok, evidence: $e}]' <<<"$results")"
    else
      printf 'arm %s: %s %s %s\n' "$arm" "$rule" "$([[ "$ok" == true ]] && echo OK || echo FAIL)" "$EVID"
    fi
  done <<<"$rules"

    jq -nc --arg d "$R" --arg arm "$arm" --argjson rules "$results" --argjson ok "$([[ $fails -eq 0 ]] && echo true || echo false)" \

  else

  fi
  [[ $fails -eq 0 ]]
}

if [[ -n "$RUN_DIR" ]]; then
  [[ -d "$RUN_DIR" ]] || usage "run dir not found: $RUN_DIR"
  rc=0; check_run "$RUN_DIR" || rc=$?
  exit "$rc"
fi

[[ -d "$BATCH_DIR" ]] || usage "batch dir not found: $BATCH_DIR"
runs=0 failed=0
while IFS= read -r d; do
  runs=$((runs + 1))
  rc=0; check_run "$d" || rc=$?

  [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || failed=$((failed + 1))

=== tools/gen-checksums.sh
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/gen-checksums.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.1, DEC-0368)
     4	#
     5	# Writes the System Zone integrity manifest `.claude/checksums.json` from the
     6	# TRACKED `.claude/` tree only. The legacy generators (mount-loa.sh and
     7	# update.sh `generate_checksums`) walk the working tree with `find`, so build,
     8	# cache and runtime artefacts (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `node_modules`,
     9	# `.run/`) that exist only on the generating machine end up in the manifest and
    10	# read as Missing on every fresh mount. This generator lists
    11	#
    12	#   git -C ROOT ls-files -z -- .claude
    13	#
    14	# minus every path under `.claude/overrides/` (user-owned) and minus the
    15	# manifest itself (`.claude/checksums.json`), hashes each with
    16	# `sha256_portable` (.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh) and writes
    17	#
    18	#   {"generated": "<UTC ISO-8601>", "algorithm": "sha256",
    19	#    "files": {"<path>": "<sha256 hex>", ...}}
    20	#
    21	# pretty-printed by jq (2-space), keys in `LC_ALL=C` byte order. Two runs on
    22	# the same tree are byte-identical except `generated`. The working-tree content
    23	# of each tracked path is hashed (an unstaged edit is reflected); a tracked
    24	# path deleted from the working tree is skipped with a warning on stderr.
    25	#
    26	# Usage:
    27	#   tools/gen-checksums.sh [--root DIR] [--out FILE]   # (re)generate
    28	#   tools/gen-checksums.sh --check [--root DIR] [--out FILE]
    29	#
    30	# Options:
    31	#   --root DIR   repository work tree to read (default: the git top level of
    32	#                the current directory)
    33	#   --out FILE   manifest path (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json). With
    34	#                --check this is the committed manifest that is compared.
    35	#   --check      regenerate to a temp file and compare its `files` map with
    36	#                the manifest at --out; nothing is written
    37	#   -h, --help   this text
    38	#
    39	# Exit codes:
    40	#   0  generated, or --check: the `files` maps are identical
    41	#   1  --check: drift (the first ten differing paths, each labelled added /
    42	#      removed / changed, on stderr) or the manifest is absent / not JSON
    43	#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or a tracked path name that
    44	#      cannot be represented safely (newline, tab or backslash)
    45	# =============================================================================
    46	set -euo pipefail
    47	export LC_ALL=C
    48	
    49	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    50	# shellcheck source=../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh
    51	source "${SELF_DIR}/../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
    52	
    53	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    54	die2() { echo "gen-checksums: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    55	
    56	MANIFEST_REL=".claude/checksums.json"
    57	ROOT=""
    58	OUT=""
    59	CHECK=0
    60	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    61	  case "$1" in
    62	    --check) CHECK=1; shift ;;
    63	    --root)
    64	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
    65	      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    66	    --out)
    67	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--out requires a file path"
    68	      OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    69	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    70	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    71	  esac
    72	done
    73	
    74	if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
    75	  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
    76	fi
    77	[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
    78	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
    79	[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
    80	  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
    81	[[ -n "$OUT" ]] || OUT="${ROOT}/${MANIFEST_REL}"
    82	
    83	TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gen-checksums.XXXXXX")"
    84	cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
    85	trap cleanup EXIT
    86	
    87	# --- 1. the tracked set (NUL-safe, C-sorted, overrides and manifest removed) --
    88	files=()
    89	while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do
    90	  case "$path" in
    91	    .claude/overrides/*|"$MANIFEST_REL") continue ;;
    92	  esac
    93	  case "$path" in
    94	    *$'\n'*|*$'\t'*|*\\*) die2 "refusing a tracked path with a newline, tab or backslash: $(printf '%q' "$path")" ;;
    95	  esac
    96	  if [[ ! -f "${ROOT}/${path}" ]]; then
    97	    # A gitlink, a dangling symlink or a path deleted in the working tree.
    98	    echo "gen-checksums: warning: tracked path not a file in the working tree, skipped: $path" >&2
    99	    continue
   100	  fi
   101	  files+=("$path")
   102	done < <(git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -z -- .claude | sort -z)
   103	
   104	# --- 2. hash in chunks (one sha256 process per 400 paths, order preserved) ----
   105	TSV="${TMP_DIR}/files.tsv"
   106	: > "$TSV"
   107	n=${#files[@]}
   108	i=0
   109	while [[ $i -lt $n ]]; do
   110	  chunk=("${files[@]:i:400}")
   111	  hashes=()
   112	  while IFS= read -r line; do
   113	    hashes+=("${line%% *}")
   114	  done < <(cd "$ROOT" && sha256_portable "${chunk[@]}")
   115	  [[ ${#hashes[@]} -eq ${#chunk[@]} ]] || die2 "sha256 returned ${#hashes[@]} digests for ${#chunk[@]} paths"
   116	  j=0
   117	  while [[ $j -lt ${#chunk[@]} ]]; do
   118	    [[ "${hashes[j]}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || die2 "unexpected sha256 output for ${chunk[j]}"
   119	    printf '%s\t%s\n' "${chunk[j]}" "${hashes[j]}" >> "$TSV"
   120	    j=$((j + 1))
   121	  done
   122	  i=$((i + 400))
   123	done
   124	[[ $n -gt 0 ]] || echo "gen-checksums: warning: no tracked files under .claude in $ROOT" >&2
   125	
   126	GEN="${TMP_DIR}/checksums.json"
   127	jq -Rn --arg generated "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '
   128	  {generated: $generated, algorithm: "sha256",
   129	   files: ([inputs | select(length > 0) | split("\t") | {key: .[0], value: .[1]}] | from_entries)}
   130	' < "$TSV" > "$GEN"
   131	
   132	# --- 3a. write ----------------------------------------------------------------
   133	if [[ $CHECK -eq 0 ]]; then
   134	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
   135	  chmod 0644 "$GEN"
   136	  # mv replaces a symlinked manifest instead of writing through it.
   137	  mv -f "$GEN" "$OUT"
   138	  echo "gen-checksums: wrote $n entries to $OUT" >&2
   139	  exit 0
   140	fi
   141	
   142	# --- 3b. --check --------------------------------------------------------------
   143	if [[ ! -f "$OUT" ]]; then
   144	  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest not found: $OUT (run tools/gen-checksums.sh)" >&2
   145	  exit 1
   146	fi
   147	if ! jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$OUT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   148	  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest is not JSON with a files object: $OUT" >&2
   149	  exit 1
   150	fi
   151	DIFF="${TMP_DIR}/diff.txt"
   152	jq -rn --slurpfile old "$OUT" --slurpfile new "$GEN" '
   153	  ($old[0].files) as $o | ($new[0].files) as $n |
   154	  ( [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select($o | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "added"} ]
   155	  + [ $o | keys[] | . as $p | select($n | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "removed"} ]
   156	  + [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select(($o | has($p)) and $o[$p] != $n[$p]) | {p: $p, k: "changed"} ] )
   157	  | sort_by(.p) | .[] | "\(.k): \(.p)"
   158	' > "$DIFF"
   159	count=$(wc -l < "$DIFF" | tr -d ' ')
   160	if [[ "$count" -eq 0 ]]; then
   161	  echo "gen-checksums: --check: OK ($n entries match $OUT)" >&2
   162	  exit 0
   163	fi
   164	echo "gen-checksums: --check: DRIFT — $count path(s) differ between $OUT and the tracked tree:" >&2
   165	sed -n '1,10s/^/  /p' "$DIFF" >&2
   166	[[ "$count" -le 10 ]] || echo "  ... and $((count - 10)) more" >&2
   167	echo "gen-checksums: regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
   168	exit 1
=== tools/check-manifest-paths.sh
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-manifest-paths.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.2, DEC-0368)
     4	#
     5	# CI gate for the System Zone integrity manifest: every path listed in
     6	# `.claude/checksums.json` must be TRACKED (`git ls-files -- .claude`) and
     7	# PRESENT in the working tree. A manifest generated by walking a dirty tree
     8	# (the #1267 class) lists build, cache and runtime artefacts that no fresh
     9	# mount has, so every downstream `check-loa.sh` reports them as Missing.
    10	#
    11	# Offenders are grouped on stderr:
    12	#   untracked  — listed in the manifest, not in `git ls-files`; each carries a
    13	#                DIAGNOSTIC class (first match wins):
    14	#                  __pycache__ | .pytest_cache | node_modules | .run
    15	#                      (a path component of that name)
    16	#                  .pyc   (name ends in .pyc)
    17	#                  .lock  (name ends in .lock)
    18	#                  other
    19	#   missing    — tracked, but absent from the working tree
    20	# The classes label untracked offenders only: a TRACKED path is never flagged
    21	# for its name (a committed `.lock` fixture is legitimate).
    22	#
    23	# Last line on stdout:
    24	#   manifest-paths: N entries, M untracked (class=count, ...), K missing
    25	#
    26	# Usage:
    27	#   tools/check-manifest-paths.sh [--manifest FILE] [--root DIR]
    28	#
    29	# Options:
    30	#   --root DIR       repository work tree (default: the git top level of the
    31	#                    current directory)
    32	#   --manifest FILE  manifest to check (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json)
    33	#   -h, --help       this text
    34	#
    35	# Exit codes:
    36	#   0  every manifest path is tracked and present
    37	#   1  at least one untracked or missing path (listed on stderr)
    38	#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or the manifest is absent or
    39	#      not JSON with a `files` object
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die2() { echo "check-manifest-paths: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    46	
    47	ROOT=""
    48	MANIFEST=""
    49	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    50	  case "$1" in
    51	    --root)
    52	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
    53	      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    54	    --manifest)
    55	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--manifest requires a file path"
    56	      MANIFEST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    57	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    58	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    59	  esac
    60	done
    61	
    62	if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
    63	  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
    64	fi
    65	[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
    66	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
    67	[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
    68	  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
    69	[[ -n "$MANIFEST" ]] || MANIFEST="${ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json"
    70	[[ -f "$MANIFEST" ]] || die2 "manifest not found: $MANIFEST"
    71	jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$MANIFEST" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    72	  || die2 "manifest is not JSON with a files object: $MANIFEST"
    73	
    74	TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-manifest-paths.XXXXXX")"
    75	cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
    76	trap cleanup EXIT
    77	
    78	# Both lists newline-separated and C-sorted. A path with a newline cannot be
    79	# represented in either list; gen-checksums.sh refuses to emit one.
    80	git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- .claude | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/tracked"
    81	jq -r '.files | keys[]' "$MANIFEST" | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/listed"
    82	comm -23 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
    83	comm -12 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/both"
    84	
    85	classify() {
    86	  local p="$1"
    87	  if [[ "$p" =~ (^|/)(__pycache__|\.pytest_cache|node_modules|\.run)(/|$) ]]; then
    88	    printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    89	  elif [[ "$p" == *.pyc ]]; then
    90	    printf '.pyc'
    91	  elif [[ "$p" == *.lock ]]; then
    92	    printf '.lock'
    93	  else
    94	    printf 'other'
    95	  fi
    96	}
    97	
    98	# Classified untracked offenders: "<class>\t<path>"
    99	: > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls"
   100	while IFS= read -r p; do
   101	  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
   102	  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(classify "$p")" "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls"
   103	done < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
   104	
   105	: > "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
   106	while IFS= read -r p; do
   107	  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
   108	  [[ -e "${ROOT}/${p}" ]] || printf '%s\n' "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
   109	done < "${TMP_DIR}/both"
   110	
   111	entries=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/listed" | tr -d ' ')
   112	n_untracked=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" | tr -d ' ')
   113	n_missing=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/missing" | tr -d ' ')
   114	
   115	class_summary=""
   116	if [[ "$n_untracked" -gt 0 ]]; then
   117	  echo "check-manifest-paths: untracked manifest paths (not in git ls-files -- .claude), by class:" >&2
   118	  for cls in __pycache__ .pytest_cache node_modules .run .pyc .lock other; do
   119	    c=$(awk -F'\t' -v c="$cls" '$1 == c' "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
   120	    [[ "$c" -gt 0 ]] || continue
   121	    class_summary="${class_summary:+${class_summary}, }${cls}=${c}"
   122	    echo "  [${cls}] ${c} path(s):" >&2
   123	    awk -F'\t' -v c="$cls" '$1 == c { print "    " $2 }' "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" >&2
   124	  done
   125	fi
   126	if [[ "$n_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
   127	  echo "check-manifest-paths: tracked manifest paths absent from the working tree:" >&2
   128	  sed 's/^/    /' "${TMP_DIR}/missing" >&2
   129	fi
   130	
   131	echo "manifest-paths: ${entries} entries, ${n_untracked} untracked${class_summary:+ (${class_summary})}, ${n_missing} missing"
   132	if [[ "$n_untracked" -gt 0 || "$n_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
   133	  echo "check-manifest-paths: FAIL — regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
   134	  exit 1
   135	fi
   136	exit 0

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.4, AC-1.3)
     4	#
     5	# Proves that a FRESH downstream submodule mount of this repository passes
     6	# `check-loa.sh` integrity: no Tampered, no Missing (paths the mount does not
     7	# link by design are reported as not-mounted and do not fail).
     8	#
     9	# Steps, all inside a new temp directory (nothing outside it is written):
    10	#   1. upstream/   — a `git clone` of this repository over file://, with a
    11	#                    local branch `fresh-mount-proof` at REF. With --worktree
    12	#                    the source work tree's uncommitted state (tracked edits,
    13	#                    deletions and untracked non-ignored files) is copied in
    14	#                    and committed on that branch, inside the temp clone only.
    15	#   2. downstream/ — `git init`, one commit, then the downstream entry point
    16	#                    `upstream/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh --branch
    17	#                    fresh-mount-proof --ref <sha> --force` with
    18	#                    LOA_UPSTREAM=file://.../upstream (the mount clones the
    19	#                    submodule from there; no network).
    20	#   3. `aleph.enabled: false` is set in downstream/.loa.config.yaml.
    21	#   4. `bash .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh` runs in downstream/; its full output
    22	#      is printed, then a summary line
    23	#        fresh-mount-proof: Tampered=T Missing=M not-mounted=N check-loa-rc=R
    24	#
    25	# Git runs hermetically: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1,
    26	# a fixed identity, protocol.file.allow=always (needed for a file:// submodule
    27	# on git >= 2.38.1) and core.hooksPath pointed at an empty directory.
    28	#
    29	# Usage:
    30	#   tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh [--ref REF] [--worktree] [--keep] [--tmp DIR]
    31	#
    32	# Options:
    33	#   --ref REF    commit-ish of this repository to mount (default: HEAD of the
    34	#                repository the script lives in)
    35	#   --worktree   mount REF plus the source work tree's uncommitted state
    36	#                (use before the change is committed)
    37	#   --keep       keep the temp directory and print its path
    38	#   --tmp DIR    parent directory for the temp directory (default: $TMPDIR or
    39	#                /tmp)
    40	#   -h, --help   this text
    41	#
    42	# Exit codes:
    43	#   0    check-loa.sh exited 0 on the fresh mount
    44	#   1    check-loa.sh exited non-zero (its output names the failures)
    45	#   2    usage error
    46	#   3    setup failed (clone, overlay, downstream init or the mount itself);
    47	#        the failing step's output is printed
    48	# =============================================================================
    49	set -euo pipefail
    50	export LC_ALL=C
    51	
    52	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    53	die2() { echo "fresh-mount-proof: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    54	die3() { echo "fresh-mount-proof: SETUP FAILED: $*" >&2; exit 3; }
    55	
    56	REF=""
    57	KEEP=0
    58	WORKTREE=0
    59	TMP_PARENT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
    60	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    61	  case "$1" in
    62	    --ref)
    63	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--ref requires a commit-ish"
    64	      REF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    65	    --tmp)
    66	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--tmp requires a directory"
    67	      TMP_PARENT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    68	    --keep) KEEP=1; shift ;;
    69	    --worktree) WORKTREE=1; shift ;;
    70	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    71	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    72	  esac
    73	done
    74	[[ -d "$TMP_PARENT" ]] || die2 "--tmp is not a directory: $TMP_PARENT"
    75	
    76	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)"
    77	SRC="$(git -C "$SELF_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "script is not inside a git work tree"
    78	[[ -n "$REF" ]] || REF="HEAD"
    79	REF_SHA="$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${REF}^{commit}")" || die2 "not a commit in $SRC: $REF"
    80	
    81	WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMP_PARENT%/}/fresh-mount-proof.XXXXXX")"
    82	cleanup() {
    83	  if [[ $KEEP -eq 1 ]]; then
    84	    echo "fresh-mount-proof: kept $WORK" >&2
    85	  else
    86	    rm -rf "$WORK"
    87	  fi
    88	}
    89	trap cleanup EXIT
    90	
    91	# --- hermetic git ---------------------------------------------------------------
    92	mkdir -p "$WORK/no-hooks"
    93	export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
    94	export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3
    95	export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=protocol.file.allow GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=always
    96	export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1="$WORK/no-hooks"
    97	export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2=init.defaultBranch GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2=main
    98	export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="fresh-mount-proof" GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="fresh-mount-proof@localhost"
    99	export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="$GIT_AUTHOR_NAME" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="$GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL"
   100	unset LOA_ALEPH_ENABLED
   101	
   102	LOG="$WORK/step.log"
   103	run_step() {  # run_step <description> <cmd...>; output to $LOG, printed on failure
   104	  local desc="$1"; shift
   105	  if ! "$@" > "$LOG" 2>&1; then
   106	    cat "$LOG" >&2
   107	    die3 "$desc"
   108	  fi
   109	}
   110	
   111	suffix=""
   112	[[ $WORKTREE -eq 1 ]] && suffix=" + work-tree state"
   113	echo "fresh-mount-proof: source $SRC at ${REF_SHA}${suffix}"
   114	echo "fresh-mount-proof: temp dir $WORK"
   115	
   116	# --- 1. upstream clone ----------------------------------------------------------
   117	UP="$WORK/upstream"
   118	run_step "clone $SRC" git clone --quiet --no-checkout "file://$SRC" "$UP"
   119	run_step "fetch $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" fetch --quiet origin "$REF_SHA"
   120	run_step "branch at $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" checkout --quiet -B fresh-mount-proof "$REF_SHA"
   121	
   122	overlay() {
   123	  local p
   124	  while IFS= read -r -d '' p; do
   125	    if [[ -e "$SRC/$p" || -L "$SRC/$p" ]]; then
   126	      [[ -d "$SRC/$p" && ! -L "$SRC/$p" ]] && continue   # gitlink / nested repo
   127	      mkdir -p "$UP/$(dirname "$p")"
   128	      rm -f "$UP/$p"
   129	      cp -P "$SRC/$p" "$UP/$p"
   130	    else
   131	      rm -f "$UP/$p"
   132	    fi
   133	  done < <(git -C "$SRC" ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard)
   134	  git -C "$UP" add -A
   135	  git -C "$UP" commit --quiet --allow-empty -m "fresh-mount-proof: work-tree state of $SRC"
   136	}
   137	[[ $WORKTREE -eq 1 ]] && run_step "work-tree overlay" overlay
   138	MOUNT_SHA="$(git -C "$UP" rev-parse HEAD)"
   139	echo "fresh-mount-proof: mounting upstream commit $MOUNT_SHA"
   140	
   141	# --- 2. downstream repository and the submodule mount --------------------------
   142	DOWN="$WORK/downstream"
   143	mkdir -p "$DOWN"
   144	init_downstream() {
   145	  git -C "$DOWN" init --quiet
   146	  printf '# downstream fixture\n' > "$DOWN/README.md"
   147	  git -C "$DOWN" add README.md
   148	  git -C "$DOWN" commit --quiet -m "initial commit"
   149	}
   150	run_step "downstream init" init_downstream
   151	
   152	do_mount() {
   153	  (cd "$DOWN" && LOA_UPSTREAM="file://$UP" bash "$UP/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh" \
   154	    --branch fresh-mount-proof --ref "$MOUNT_SHA" --force < /dev/null)
   155	}
   156	run_step "mount-submodule.sh" do_mount
   157	echo "fresh-mount-proof: mount-submodule.sh exited 0 ($(grep -c 'Linked' "$LOG" || true) link lines)"
   158	
   159	# --- 3. Aleph off ---------------------------------------------------------------
   160	CFG="$DOWN/.loa.config.yaml"
   161	[[ -f "$CFG" ]] || : > "$CFG"
   162	if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   163	  run_step "aleph.enabled: false" yq -i '.aleph.enabled = false' "$CFG"
   164	else
   165	  printf '\naleph:\n  enabled: false\n' >> "$CFG"
   166	fi
   167	
   168	# --- 4. check-loa.sh ------------------------------------------------------------
   169	OUT="$WORK/check-loa.out"
   170	rc=0
   171	(cd "$DOWN" && CI=true bash .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh < /dev/null) > "$OUT" 2>&1 || rc=$?
   172	echo "----- check-loa.sh (downstream) -----"
   173	cat "$OUT"
   174	echo "----- end check-loa.sh (exit $rc) -----"
   175	
   176	tampered=$(grep -c 'Tampered: ' "$OUT" || true)
   177	missing=$(grep -c 'Missing: ' "$OUT" || true)
   178	not_mounted=$(sed -n 's/.*not-mounted: \([0-9][0-9]*\) path(s).*/\1/p' "$OUT")
   179	echo "fresh-mount-proof: Tampered=${tampered} Missing=${missing} not-mounted=${not_mounted:-0} check-loa-rc=${rc}"
   180	[[ $rc -eq 0 ]] && exit 0
   181	exit 1

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/gen-checksums.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.1, DEC-0368)
     4	#
     5	# Writes the System Zone integrity manifest `.claude/checksums.json` from the
     6	# TRACKED `.claude/` tree only. The legacy generators (mount-loa.sh and
     7	# update.sh `generate_checksums`) walk the working tree with `find`, so build,
     8	# cache and runtime artefacts (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `node_modules`,
     9	# `.run/`) that exist only on the generating machine end up in the manifest and
    10	# read as Missing on every fresh mount. This generator lists
    11	#
    12	#   git -C ROOT ls-files -z -- .claude
    13	#
    14	# minus every path under `.claude/overrides/` (user-owned) and minus the
    15	# manifest itself (`.claude/checksums.json`), hashes each with
    16	# `sha256_portable` (.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh) and writes
    17	#
    18	#   {"generated": "<UTC ISO-8601>", "algorithm": "sha256",
    19	#    "files": {"<path>": "<sha256 hex>", ...}}
    20	#
    21	# pretty-printed by jq (2-space), keys in `LC_ALL=C` byte order. Two runs on
    22	# the same tree are byte-identical except `generated`. The working-tree content
    23	# of each tracked path is hashed (an unstaged edit is reflected); a tracked
    24	# path deleted from the working tree is skipped with a warning on stderr.
    25	#
    26	# Usage:
    27	#   tools/gen-checksums.sh [--root DIR] [--out FILE]   # (re)generate
    28	#   tools/gen-checksums.sh --check [--root DIR] [--out FILE]
    29	#
    30	# Options:
    31	#   --root DIR   repository work tree to read (default: the git top level of
    32	#                the current directory)
    33	#   --out FILE   manifest path (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json). With
    34	#                --check this is the committed manifest that is compared.
    35	#   --check      regenerate to a temp file and compare its `files` map with
    36	#                the manifest at --out; nothing is written
    37	#   -h, --help   this text
    38	#
    39	# Exit codes:
    40	#   0  generated, or --check: the `files` maps are identical
    41	#   1  --check: drift (the first ten differing paths, each labelled added /
    42	#      removed / changed, on stderr) or the manifest is absent / not JSON
    43	#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or a tracked path name that
    44	#      cannot be represented safely (newline, tab or backslash)
    45	# =============================================================================
    46	set -euo pipefail
    47	export LC_ALL=C
    48	
    49	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    50	# shellcheck source=../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh
    51	source "${SELF_DIR}/../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
    52	
    53	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    54	die2() { echo "gen-checksums: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    55	
    56	MANIFEST_REL=".claude/checksums.json"
    57	ROOT=""
    58	OUT=""
    59	CHECK=0
    60	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    61	  case "$1" in
    62	    --check) CHECK=1; shift ;;
    63	    --root)
    64	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
    65	      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    66	    --out)
    67	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--out requires a file path"
    68	      OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    69	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    70	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    71	  esac
    72	done
    73	
    74	if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
    75	  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
    76	fi
    77	[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
    78	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
    79	[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
    80	  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
    81	[[ -n "$OUT" ]] || OUT="${ROOT}/${MANIFEST_REL}"
    82	
    83	TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gen-checksums.XXXXXX")"
    84	cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
    85	trap cleanup EXIT
    86	
    87	# --- 1. the tracked set (NUL-safe, C-sorted, overrides and manifest removed) --
    88	files=()
    89	while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do
    90	  case "$path" in
    91	    .claude/overrides/*|"$MANIFEST_REL") continue ;;
    92	  esac
    93	  case "$path" in
    94	    *$'\n'*|*$'\t'*|*\\*) die2 "refusing a tracked path with a newline, tab or backslash: $(printf '%q' "$path")" ;;
    95	  esac
    96	  if [[ ! -f "${ROOT}/${path}" ]]; then
    97	    # A gitlink, a dangling symlink or a path deleted in the working tree.
    98	    echo "gen-checksums: warning: tracked path not a file in the working tree, skipped: $path" >&2
    99	    continue
   100	  fi
   101	  files+=("$path")
   102	done < <(git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -z -- .claude | sort -z)
   103	
   104	# --- 2. hash in chunks (one sha256 process per 400 paths, order preserved) ----
   105	TSV="${TMP_DIR}/files.tsv"
   106	: > "$TSV"
   107	n=${#files[@]}
   108	i=0
   109	while [[ $i -lt $n ]]; do
   110	  chunk=("${files[@]:i:400}")
   111	  hashes=()
   112	  while IFS= read -r line; do
   113	    hashes+=("${line%% *}")
   114	  done < <(cd "$ROOT" && sha256_portable "${chunk[@]}")
   115	  [[ ${#hashes[@]} -eq ${#chunk[@]} ]] || die2 "sha256 returned ${#hashes[@]} digests for ${#chunk[@]} paths"
   116	  j=0
   117	  while [[ $j -lt ${#chunk[@]} ]]; do
   118	    [[ "${hashes[j]}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || die2 "unexpected sha256 output for ${chunk[j]}"
   119	    printf '%s\t%s\n' "${chunk[j]}" "${hashes[j]}" >> "$TSV"
   120	    j=$((j + 1))
   121	  done
   122	  i=$((i + 400))
   123	done
   124	[[ $n -gt 0 ]] || echo "gen-checksums: warning: no tracked files under .claude in $ROOT" >&2
   125	
   126	GEN="${TMP_DIR}/checksums.json"
   127	jq -Rn --arg generated "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '
   128	  {generated: $generated, algorithm: "sha256",
   129	   files: ([inputs | select(length > 0) | split("\t") | {key: .[0], value: .[1]}] | from_entries)}
   130	' < "$TSV" > "$GEN"
   131	
   132	# --- 3a. write ----------------------------------------------------------------
   133	if [[ $CHECK -eq 0 ]]; then
   134	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
   135	  chmod 0644 "$GEN"
   136	  # mv replaces a symlinked manifest instead of writing through it.
   137	  mv -f "$GEN" "$OUT"
   138	  echo "gen-checksums: wrote $n entries to $OUT" >&2
   139	  exit 0
   140	fi
   141	
   142	# --- 3b. --check --------------------------------------------------------------
   143	if [[ ! -f "$OUT" ]]; then
   144	  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest not found: $OUT (run tools/gen-checksums.sh)" >&2
   145	  exit 1
   146	fi
   147	if ! jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$OUT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   148	  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest is not JSON with a files object: $OUT" >&2
   149	  exit 1
   150	fi
   151	DIFF="${TMP_DIR}/diff.txt"
   152	jq -rn --slurpfile old "$OUT" --slurpfile new "$GEN" '
   153	  ($old[0].files) as $o | ($new[0].files) as $n |
   154	  ( [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select($o | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "added"} ]
   155	  + [ $o | keys[] | . as $p | select($n | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "removed"} ]
   156	  + [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select(($o | has($p)) and $o[$p] != $n[$p]) | {p: $p, k: "changed"} ] )
   157	  | sort_by(.p) | .[] | "\(.k): \(.p)"
   158	' > "$DIFF"
   159	count=$(wc -l < "$DIFF" | tr -d ' ')
   160	if [[ "$count" -eq 0 ]]; then
   161	  echo "gen-checksums: --check: OK ($n entries match $OUT)" >&2
   162	  exit 0
   163	fi
   164	echo "gen-checksums: --check: DRIFT — $count path(s) differ between $OUT and the tracked tree:" >&2
   165	sed -n '1,10s/^/  /p' "$DIFF" >&2
   166	[[ "$count" -le 10 ]] || echo "  ... and $((count - 10)) more" >&2
   167	echo "gen-checksums: regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
   168	exit 1

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-manifest-paths.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.2, DEC-0368)
     4	#
     5	# CI gate for the System Zone integrity manifest: every path listed in
     6	# `.claude/checksums.json` must be TRACKED (`git ls-files -- .claude`) and
     7	# PRESENT in the working tree. A manifest generated by walking a dirty tree
     8	# (the #1267 class) lists build, cache and runtime artefacts that no fresh
     9	# mount has, so every downstream `check-loa.sh` reports them as Missing.
    10	#
    11	# Offenders are grouped on stderr:
    12	#   untracked  — listed in the manifest, not in `git ls-files`; each carries a
    13	#                DIAGNOSTIC class (first match wins):
    14	#                  __pycache__ | .pytest_cache | node_modules | .run
    15	#                      (a path component of that name)
    16	#                  .pyc   (name ends in .pyc)
    17	#                  .lock  (name ends in .lock)
    18	#                  other
    19	#   missing    — tracked, but absent from the working tree
    20	# The classes label untracked offenders only: a TRACKED path is never flagged
    21	# for its name (a committed `.lock` fixture is legitimate).
    22	#
    23	# Last line on stdout:
    24	#   manifest-paths: N entries, M untracked (class=count, ...), K missing
    25	#
    26	# Usage:
    27	#   tools/check-manifest-paths.sh [--manifest FILE] [--root DIR]
    28	#
    29	# Options:
    30	#   --root DIR       repository work tree (default: the git top level of the
    31	#                    current directory)
    32	#   --manifest FILE  manifest to check (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json)
    33	#   -h, --help       this text
    34	#
    35	# Exit codes:
    36	#   0  every manifest path is tracked and present
    37	#   1  at least one untracked or missing path (listed on stderr)
    38	#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or the manifest is absent or
    39	#      not JSON with a `files` object
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die2() { echo "check-manifest-paths: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    46	
    47	ROOT=""
    48	MANIFEST=""
    49	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    50	  case "$1" in
    51	    --root)
    52	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
    53	      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    54	    --manifest)
    55	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--manifest requires a file path"
    56	      MANIFEST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    57	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    58	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    59	  esac
    60	done
    61	
    62	if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
    63	  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
    64	fi
    65	[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
    66	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
    67	[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
    68	  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
    69	[[ -n "$MANIFEST" ]] || MANIFEST="${ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json"
    70	[[ -f "$MANIFEST" ]] || die2 "manifest not found: $MANIFEST"
    71	jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$MANIFEST" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    72	  || die2 "manifest is not JSON with a files object: $MANIFEST"
    73	
    74	TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-manifest-paths.XXXXXX")"
    75	cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
    76	trap cleanup EXIT
    77	
    78	# Both lists newline-separated and C-sorted. A path with a newline cannot be
    79	# represented in either list; gen-checksums.sh refuses to emit one.
    80	git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- .claude | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/tracked"
    81	jq -r '.files | keys[]' "$MANIFEST" | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/listed"
    82	comm -23 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
    83	comm -12 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/both"
    84	
    85	classify() {
    86	  local p="$1"
    87	  if [[ "$p" =~ (^|/)(__pycache__|\.pytest_cache|node_modules|\.run)(/|$) ]]; then
    88	    printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    89	  elif [[ "$p" == *.pyc ]]; then
    90	    printf '.pyc'
    91	  elif [[ "$p" == *.lock ]]; then
    92	    printf '.lock'
    93	  else
    94	    printf 'other'
    95	  fi

     6	# "<sha256>  <relpath>" line per file under <root>/tasks/ (and <root>/smoke/

     9	# validate-suite.sh runs first; an invalid suite is never frozen or accepted.
    10	#
    11	# Usage:
    12	#   freeze.sh [--root DIR] [--smoke] [--check] [--allow-partial] [--suite-file F]
    13	#
    14	#   --root DIR        suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0)
    15	#   --smoke           cover smoke/ too (passed to the validator as well)
    16	#   --check           recompute and compare with MANIFEST.sha256; write nothing
    17	#   --allow-partial   passed to validate-suite.sh (fewer than four tasks per type)
    18	#   --suite-file F    passed to validate-suite.sh
    19	#
    20	# Output: `freeze: wrote MANIFEST.sha256 (N files, sha256 <digest of the manifest>)`
    21	# or `freeze: OK — N files match MANIFEST.sha256 (sha256 …)`; on drift every
    22	# changed / added / removed path on its own line.
    23	#
    24	# Exit: 0 written / matches; 1 drift, missing manifest under --check, or the
    25	#       validator found violations; 2 usage.

    27	# =============================================================================

    29	export LC_ALL=C
    30	
    31	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    32	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    33	
    34	ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0"
    35	CHECK=false SMOKE=false
    36	VARGS=()

    39	die() { echo "freeze: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    40	
    41	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    42	  case "$1" in
    43	    --root) ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    44	    --smoke) SMOKE=true; VARGS+=(--smoke); shift ;;
    45	    --check) CHECK=true; shift ;;
    46	    --allow-partial) VARGS+=(--allow-partial); shift ;;
    47	    --suite-file) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || die "--suite-file needs a path"; VARGS+=(--suite-file "$2"); shift 2 ;;
    48	    --help|-h) usage ;;

    55

    62	compute_manifest() {

   102	def load(p):
   103	    m = {}
   104	    for line in open(p, encoding="utf-8"):

   107	            h, _, rel = line.partition("  ")

   110	old, new = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])

   113	        print(f"  removed  {rel}")
   114	    elif rel not in old:
   115	        print(f"  added    {rel}")
   116	    elif old[rel] != new[rel]:
   117	        print(f"  changed  {rel}")
   118	PY

   120	fi

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# fingerprint.sh — toolchain fingerprint for ablation runs (cycle-130 FR-4, SDD A11 / DEC-0389)
     4	#
     5	# Prints `fp:<sha256>` over the LC_ALL=C-sorted `tool=version` lines of the
     6	# toolchain an ablation run depends on (claude, codex, python3, node, yq, jq,
     7	# bats, git, docker) plus `source_tree=<HEAD of --source-tree>`. A tool that is
     8	# not installed reads `tool=absent`, so a missing tool changes the fingerprint
     9	# instead of failing the run. The value fills `image_digest` in host mode and
    10	# `fingerprint` in every mode (MANIFEST.json, pipeline.json, runs.jsonl). It reads the
    11	# HOST toolchain: in container mode the phases run on the image's toolchain, and the
    12	# image digest (not this value) identifies the batch's versions (on 2026-10-15 the host
    13	# CLI was 2.1.300 while Dockerfile.ablation pins 2.1.299).
    14	#
    15	# Usage:
    16	#   fingerprint.sh [--source-tree DIR] [--claude-bin B] [--bats-bin B] [--json]
    17	#
    18	# Options:
    19	#   --source-tree DIR  the pinned Loa tree; its `git rev-parse HEAD` is folded in
    20	#                      (`none` when absent or not a git tree)
    21	#   --claude-bin B     the CLI executable (default: $EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN, else claude)
    22	#   --bats-bin B       bats executable (default: bats on PATH, else the operator's
    23	#                      ~/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats)
    24	#   --json             print {fingerprint, tools{}, source_tree, lines[]} instead
    25	#
    26	# Exit codes:
    27	#   0  printed
    28	#   2  usage error
    29	#
    30	# Tested by evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats (fingerprint cases).
    31	# =============================================================================
    32	set -euo pipefail
    33	export LC_ALL=C
    34	
    35	# Hashing is Python hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code (eval.yml
    36	# "Validate grader trust boundary").
    37	
    38	SOURCE_TREE=""
    39	CLAUDE_BIN="${EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN:-claude}"
    40	BATS_BIN="${LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN:-}"
    41	JSON=false
    42	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    43	  case "$1" in
    44	    --source-tree) SOURCE_TREE="${2:?--source-tree needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    45	    --claude-bin)  CLAUDE_BIN="${2:?--claude-bin needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    46	    --bats-bin)    BATS_BIN="${2:?--bats-bin needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    47	    --json)        JSON=true; shift ;;
    48	    -h|--help)     sed -n '2,28p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    49	    *) echo "fingerprint.sh: unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    50	  esac
    51	done
    52	if [[ -z "$BATS_BIN" ]]; then
    53	  if command -v bats >/dev/null 2>&1; then BATS_BIN=bats
    54	  else BATS_BIN="$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats"; fi
    55	fi

    57	# first line of `<bin> <args>`, whitespace collapsed; `absent` when not runnable

    59	  local bin="$1"; shift
    60	  if ! command -v "$bin" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ ! -x "$bin" ]]; then printf 'absent'; return 0; fi

    62	  out="$("$bin" "$@" 2>&1 < /dev/null || true)"
    63	  out="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '1p' | tr -s ' \t' ' ' | sed 's/^ //; s/ $//')"

    71	    printf 'codex=%s\n'   "$(tool_version codex --version)"
    72	    printf 'python3=%s\n' "$(tool_version python3 --version)"
    73	    printf 'node=%s\n'    "$(tool_version node --version)"
    74	    printf 'yq=%s\n'      "$(tool_version yq --version)"
    75	    printf 'jq=%s\n'      "$(tool_version jq --version)"
    76	    printf 'bats=%s\n'    "$(tool_version "$BATS_BIN" --version)"
    77	    printf 'git=%s\n'     "$(tool_version git --version)"

+    print_screen_table

# Structured Finding Output Schema

Defines the JSONL output format for machine-parseable audit findings.

## Finding Schema

Each finding is a JSON object on a single line in the JSONL file.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "AuditFinding",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "category", "criterion", "severity", "score", "finding", "reasoning_trace", "confidence"],
  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[A-Z]{2,4}-[0-9]{3}$",
      "description": "Unique finding ID (e.g., SEC-001, ARCH-042)"
    },
    "category": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["security", "architecture", "code_quality", "devops", "blockchain"],
      "description": "Audit category"
    },
    "criterion": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Specific rubric dimension (e.g., input_validation, modularity)"
    },
    "severity": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["CRITICAL", "HIGH", "MEDIUM", "LOW", "INFO"],
      "description": "Finding severity"
    },
    "score": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "maximum": 5,
      "description": "Rubric score for this dimension"
    },
    "file": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "File path where issue was found"
    },
    "line": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Line number (if applicable)"
    },
    "code_snippet": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Relevant code excerpt"
    },
    "reasoning_trace": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "How the issue was discovered - analysis path and evidence"
    },
    "finding": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Clear description of the issue"
    },
    "critique": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Specific guidance for improvement"
    },
    "remediation": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Exact fix with code example if applicable"
    },
    "confidence": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["high", "medium", "low"],
      "description": "Confidence in the finding"
    },
    "references": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {"type": "string"},
      "description": "CVE, CWE, OWASP, or other references"
    }
  }
}
```

## Example Findings

### Security Finding
```json
{"id":"SEC-001","category":"security","criterion":"input_validation","severity":"HIGH","score":2,"file":"src/api/users.ts","line":42,"code_snippet":"const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${userId}`;","reasoning_trace":"Traced user input from req.params.userId through controller to database query. Found string interpolation in SQL query construction at L42, bypassing ORM parameterization.","finding":"SQL injection vulnerability via unsanitized userId parameter","critique":"The userId is interpolated directly into SQL string. Even if userId appears numeric, type coercion allows injection. The ORM's parameterized query feature is available but not used here.","remediation":"Replace L42 with: `const user = await db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1', [userId]);`","confidence":"high","references":["CWE-89","OWASP-A03:2021"]}
```

### Architecture Finding
```json
{"id":"ARCH-012","category":"architecture","criterion":"modularity","severity":"MEDIUM","score":3,"file":"src/services/","reasoning_trace":"Analyzed import graph and found UserService imports from PaymentService, OrderService, and NotificationService. PaymentService also imports UserService creating circular dependency detected via tsc --traceResolution.","finding":"Circular dependency between UserService and PaymentService","critique":"Tight coupling between these services will make testing and modification difficult. Consider extracting shared logic to a separate module or using events for decoupling.","remediation":"1. Extract shared types to src/types/\n2. Use event emitter for cross-service communication\n3. Consider domain events pattern","confidence":"high","references":["Clean Architecture","DDD Bounded Contexts"]}
```

### Code Quality Finding
```json
{"id":"CQ-007","category":"code_quality","criterion":"error_handling","severity":"LOW","score":4,"file":"src/utils/api.ts","line":78,"code_snippet":"} catch (e) { console.log(e); }","reasoning_trace":"Reviewed error handling patterns across codebase. Found 3 instances of catch blocks that only console.log errors without proper handling or re-throwing.","finding":"Silent error swallowing in API utility","critique":"Errors are logged but not handled or propagated. This makes debugging difficult and can hide critical failures in production.","remediation":"Replace with: `} catch (e) { logger.error('API call failed', { error: e, context }); throw new ApiError('Request failed', { cause: e }); }`","confidence":"medium","references":["Error Handling Best Practices"]}
```

## Output File Location

Findings should be written to:
```
grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl
```

Each `reasoning_trace` states what was analyzed, the triggering pattern, the evidence chain from input to vulnerability, and the scoring rationale.

## Summary Record

At the end of the JSONL file, include a summary record:

```json
{"type":"summary","timestamp":"2026-01-30T12:00:00Z","category_scores":{"security":3.2,"architecture":4.1,"code_quality":3.8,"devops":4.0},"overall_score":3.8,"risk_level":"MODERATE","total_findings":{"CRITICAL":0,"HIGH":2,"MEDIUM":5,"LOW":8,"INFO":3},"verdict":"CHANGES_REQUIRED"}
```

## Parsing Example

```bash
# Get all HIGH severity findings
cat findings.jsonl | jq -c 'select(.severity == "HIGH")'

# Calculate average security score
cat findings.jsonl | jq -s '[.[] | select(.category == "security") | .score] | add / length'

# Get findings for a specific file
cat findings.jsonl | jq -c 'select(.file | contains("users.ts"))'
```

## Output File Location

Findings should be written to:
```
grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl
```

Each `reasoning_trace` states what was analyzed, the triggering pattern, the evidence chain from input to vulnerability, and the scoring rationale.

## Summary Record

At the end of the JSONL file, include a summary record:

```json
{"type":"summary","timestamp":"2026-01-30T12:00:00Z","category_scores":{"security":3.2,"architecture":4.1,"code_quality":3.8,"devops":4.0},"overall_score":3.8,"risk_level":"MODERATE","total_findings":{"CRITICAL":0,"HIGH":2,"MEDIUM":5,"LOW":8,"INFO":3},"verdict":"CHANGES_REQUIRED"}
```

## Parsing Example

```bash
# Get all HIGH severity findings
cat findings.jsonl | jq -c 'select(.severity == "HIGH")'

# Calculate average security score
cat findings.jsonl | jq -s '[.[] | select(.category == "security") | .score] | add / length'

# Get findings for a specific file
```

=== .github/workflows/bats-tests.yml
     1	# =============================================================================
     2	# BATS Shell Tests
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# Runs BATS test suites for shell scripts and framework infrastructure.
     5	# Two test directories:
     6	#   - tests/unit/           — Framework unit tests (58 files)
     7	#   - .claude/scripts/tests/ — Script-level tests (20 files)

    12	# with integrity verification. This prevents supply-chain attacks where a

     1	# Dockerfile.ablation — container executor image for the cycle-130 component ablation
     2	# (SDD D-4.9 / DEC-0411). Extends Dockerfile.sandbox's pinned base and non-root user
     3	# with the Claude Code CLI, the codex CLI, pytest and bats. It holds NO credentials.
     4	# pipeline-run.sh mounts exactly two host paths: the sandbox read-write at /workspace
     5	# and a per-run writable HOME at /home/evaluser (<run>/meta/home: the codex CLI's
     6	# auth.json/config.toml copies, empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store). The
     7	# Bedrock route authenticates from AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK passed in the environment.
     8	# The image's tool versions (below) are the batch's versions: every arm runs here.
     9	#
    10	# Build (no build context is needed; nothing is COPY'd):
    11	#   docker build -t loa-ablation:258 - < evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation
    12	# Run:
    13	#   evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh --executor container --image loa-ablation:258 …
    14	#   (pipeline-run.sh passes --rm --name --user --network bridge --read-only --tmpfs /tmp
    15	#    --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2 and exactly the two mounts)
    16	#
    17	# Digest pinned 2026-02-11 (same base as Dockerfile.sandbox):
    18	#   docker manifest inspect node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim | jq '.manifests[0].digest'
    19	FROM rust:1-bookworm AS brbuild
    20	RUN cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br --locked 2>/dev/null || cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br
    21	
    22	FROM node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim@sha256:8ea90c4f037cc3c2f566eb46c53eaac005129113487eda4090058fe554578104 AS base
    23	
    24	ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.299
    25	ARG CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1
    26	ARG PYTEST_VERSION=9.0.2
    27	ARG BATS_VERSION=v1.13.0
    28	
    29	RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    30	    bash \
    31	    git \
    32	    jq \
    33	    python3 \
    34	    python3-pip \
    35	    python3-venv \
    36	    grep \
    37	    diffutils \
    38	    coreutils \
    39	    procps \
    40	    ca-certificates \
    41	    curl \
    42	    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    43	
    44	# yq (mikefarah/yq) with SHA256 integrity verification (as Dockerfile.sandbox)
    45	ARG YQ_VERSION=v4.40.5
    46	ARG YQ_SHA256_AMD64=0d6aaf1cf44a8d18fbc7ed0ef14f735a8df8d2e314c4cc0f0242d35c0a440c95
    47	ARG YQ_SHA256_ARM64=9431f0fa39a0af03a152d7fe19a86e42e9ff28d503ed4a70598f9261ec944a97
    48	RUN arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \
    49	    case "$arch" in \
    50	      amd64) yq_arch="amd64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
    51	      arm64) yq_arch="arm64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
    52	      *) echo "Unsupported architecture: $arch" && exit 1 ;; \
    53	    esac && \
    54	    curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/${YQ_VERSION}/yq_linux_${yq_arch}" \
    55	      -o /usr/local/bin/yq && \
    56	    echo "${yq_sha256}  /usr/local/bin/yq" | sha256sum -c - && \
    57	    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq
    58	
    59	# The two CLIs at the versions the fingerprint pins (exact versions, no ranges).
    60	RUN npm install -g --no-fund --no-audit \
    61	      "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION}" \
    62	      "@openai/codex@${CODEX_VERSION}" \

    69	RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "rfc8785>=0.1.4" "jsonschema>=4.21" "pyyaml>=6.0" "httpx[http2]>=0.24.0"
    70	
    71	# bats-core at the pinned tag
    72	RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch "${BATS_VERSION}" https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core.git /tmp/bats-core && \
    73	    /tmp/bats-core/install.sh /usr/local && \
    74	    rm -rf /tmp/bats-core

    84	# markdown fallback alike (lead, Sprint 258).
    85	RUN mkdir -p /home/evaluser/.aws /home/evaluser/.claude /home/evaluser/.codex /workspace && \
    86	    chown -R evaluser:evaluser /home/evaluser /workspace

    88	ENV TZ=UTC
    89	ENV LC_ALL=C
    90	ENV HOME=/home/evaluser
    91	ENV NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=true
    92	ENV CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1
    93	
    94	USER evaluser
    95	WORKDIR /workspace
    96	
    97	# Health check — every tool the fingerprint names is present
    98	RUN bash --version && git --version && jq --version && node --version && \
    99	    python3 --version && python3 -m pytest --version && yq --version && \
   100	    bats --version && claude --version && codex --version && \
   101	    echo "All tools verified"
   102	
   103	ENTRYPOINT []
   104	CMD ["/bin/bash"]

756	+    if not isinstance(t.get("id"), str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}", t.get("id") or ""):

873	+    elif suite_version is not None and sv != suite_version:

933	+    fi

941	+  cat "$WORK/report.txt"
942	+  echo "validate-suite: $violations violation(s) over $ntasks task(s) in $ROOT" >&2
943	+  exit 1
